product: MM-ART-010 parameterized permanent one-off city-map wall relief with complete water apertures, S/U transit accent and targeted topology bridges

scope.intended_use: Unique indoor decorative Berlin wall relief, produced as two four-color main prints and permanently assembled without adhesive, rear grid, magnets, or replaceable sections. Revision 0.5.4 keeps every retained mapped water area and river/canal/stream as a recognizable light-through opening, cross-checks final apertures against independent Berlin, BKG and OSM hydrography, and permits only explicitly logged local full-thickness topology bridges. Sky Blue represents S-Bahn/U-Bahn plus the existing context boundary and address-anchored site marker, and motorway/trunk remains Midnight. Each half has its own upper wall support so the center seam is not the primary gravity load path.
scope.user_context: Adult indoor customer; optional customer-supplied low-power rear halo/front-through lighting; production on the Anycubic Kobra 3 Max Combo.

failure_modes.mode: Wrong location, unreadable artwork, fifth color, or collision with protected geometry
failure_modes.effect: Misleading or visually defective one-off artwork; slice or assembly may fail
failure_modes.mitigation: Freeze geocode provenance, parameterize artwork independently, reuse one existing tool and rerun deterministic placement, feature, mesh and slicer checks

acceptance_criteria: Digital analysis confirms that the canonical stacked metriMade artwork is connected to the frozen address by an unambiguous callout anchor, measures 54.0 × 57.18 mm with aspect ratio preserved, lies on exactly one retained main half, keeps at least 50 mm from the center seam and 5 mm from the outer perimeter, does not delete named water coverage, has no printable feature below 0.9 mm, rises 0.6 mm and uses tool 4. A human recognizes it at 2.0 m under ordinary indoor lighting on a process-matched Oak/Sky Blue coupon.

failure_modes.mode: A mapped water body is omitted, a marker or protected land hides a named water body, a topology bridge interrupts a major water corridor, a water cut disconnects the backer, or a motorway occupies the transit color body
failure_modes.effect: The map is semantically inconsistent, visually defective, structurally fragmented, or unsuitable for intended backlighting
failure_modes.mitigation: Cross-check OSM against official Berlin and BKG hydrography, verify named polygon coverage and Havel corridor continuity on the final aperture and exported mesh, route marker callouts onto dry land, retain local-only bridge manifests and audit tool ownership

acceptance_criteria: The final exported aperture covers at least 90 percent of the official Tegeler See reference after raster tolerance in both modes; no marker or generic keep-out deletes named water; the final Havel opening intersects every ordered official control segment from the northern Berlin boundary through Spandauer See, Pichelssee and Wannsee with only logged local structural bridges; source agreement and every intentional deletion are reported; tool 4 contains S-/U-Bahn relations but no independent motorway accent geometry; all halves remain connected and below the 12 percent opening cap.

criticality.rationale: The artwork is decorative, but a failed printed wall interface or unsuitable customer lighting has credible injury, property-damage, or heat consequences and therefore requires controlled tests.

decision.rationale: The all-water and local-bridge architecture remains approved, but revision 0.5.3 is rejected because weak regressions did not detect final visual deletion of the Tegeler See and a Havel interruption. Revision 0.5.4 correction work may proceed only under multi-source final-aperture coverage, ordered Havel continuity, connectivity, open-area and target-slicer controls.

warnings.message: The selected canonical metriMade vector asset MM-BRAND-001-R1 is recorded as clearance pending; commercial release remains blocked.
The 54.0 mm stacked lockup targets recognition from 2.0 m, but renders and digital dimensions cannot prove human readability; a process-matched coupon is required.
The one-way connector and snap-in mounting interfaces have no exact process-qualified clearance or physical result.
Concealed seam pockets must remain printable in the face-up main-part orientation and must not create unsupported roofs or visible read-through.
The physical spool products are identified, but common-process compatibility, opacity, directed purge, conditioning, ACE slots and numeric mechanical thresholds remain unverified.

Revision 0.5.1 project files are mesh-readable but omit water-area multipolygons including Tegeler See and use Sky Blue for motorway accents; they must not be printed or released as the corrected map.
Digital connectivity does not prove handling stiffness or wall safety; the selected bridge candidate still requires a process-matched physical handling and installed proof test.
Revision 0.5.3 must not be printed: its nonzero Tegeler See test was a false positive and final visual inspection found the lake and a major Havel segment obscured by downstream keep-outs or bridges.

Official Berlin Gewässerkarte, BKG DLM250 and OSM references have been identified; immutable bounded derivatives, final-aperture agreement and Havel corridor controls must pass before replacement geometry.

next_actions.action: Freeze bounded Berlin Gewässerkarte and BKG DLM250 references alongside OSM, then quantify named water agreement.
next_actions.exit_criterion: Tegeler See and the full Berlin Havel corridor are present in at least two independent sources with immutable hashes and common-CRS bounds.

next_actions.exit_criterion: Final-aperture coverage and ordered Havel control-segment tests pass in both display modes while each half stays connected below the opening cap.
